en: The national flower, Sampaguita, blooms year-round and releases its strongest fragrance at night to attract pollinating moths.
The Philippine Eagle, our national bird, uses its heavy, dark crest to shield its eyes from rain while hunting in the canopy.
Dr. Ramon Barba discovered that spraying potassium nitrate on mango trees triggers observable flowering even during the dry season.
The Ifugao built stone-walled rice terraces that use observable gravity-fed irrigation channels to distribute water from mountain forests down to the paddies.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate homes with kiping, which are observable, colorful leaf-shaped wafers made from ground rice.
The Narra, our national tree, sheds its observable, compound leaves during the dry season to conserve water before blooming yellow flowers.
Marine biologist Angel Alcala established observable no-take coral reef sanctuaries in the Philippines to protect local fish biodiversity from overfishing.
The Hanunuo Mangyan use observable, straight-grained bamboo tubes, heated and scraped, to carve their traditional syllabic script called Surat Mangyan.
The South Sea Pearl, our national gem, forms inside the Pinctada maxima oyster through the observable biological process of nacre secretion.
The Philippine Clean Air Act mandates the observable reduction of smoke belching from jeepneys to protect citizens from harmful particulate matter.
The Tamaraw, an observable endemic dwarf buffalo, has short, V-shaped horns and distinct white facial markings to blend into Mindoro's tall grasses.
The Davao Kadayawan Festival celebrates the observable seasonal harvest of indigenous fruits like durian and pomelo from the region's volcanic soil.
